summary: All four tickets are runtime/CI/test-infrastructure only, correctly take no migration (confirmed empty diff on packages/db/migrations), and correctly leave apps/web untouched. Every numeric claim in the four per-ticket reports that could be re-run on this rig reproduced exactly on independent re-run (ready.test.mjs 25/25, rollback-preflight.test.mjs 42/20/0/22, the nine #1041 db test files 31/26/0/5, the combined operation-census+rig-isolation run, check-frozen-workflows, check-parts-parity, typecheck, and CI-mode lint), and the load-bearing vacuity controls each report describes (the marker-evidence strings actually present in lib/intake.mjs and lib/reconciler-fa.mjs; the #651/0227 vs '#932/0277' migration-attribution correction; every reviseParticulars call site already awaiting the now-async fixture) hold up against the source tree. Commit structure follows /tdd's vertical-slice discipline: each of the 13 commits pairs a described defect with its own fix and test(s) rather than separating a batch of red tests from implementation, commit messages are scoped to one ticket each and end with the house Co-Authored-By trailer, and #1041's five commits in particular are each a single, independently-measured defect (drill DB-name grammar, the x41 change_class frontier-compat, the two d-b1 censuses, the gate-chain/cell-floor mechanism, the 0041 drill's name-family fix). Docs are updated in the same commits per rule 9 (packages/db/tests/README.md, packages/runtime/README.md, and one minimal, correctly-positioned CONTEXT.md hunk for #1035's new 'Runtime contract marker' term, respecting the shared-file rule). Test quality is high: the #1035 cells are pure (an explicit frontier, a stub query) exactly where the module's own design says they should be, the #877 leg reads the admission outcome off the door's own durable `clara.op_receipts` idempotency receipt rather than the population-mismatched `sweep_run_items.outcome` column after first proving by direct measurement that the latter cannot carry an 'admitted' outcome at all, and the #1033 repro is a genuine bounded, deterministic reproduction of the named race (shown red for the right reason, then green, then re-run three times) rather than a widened timeout. No hard standards violation was found. Two low-severity, judgement-call findings are recorded below; neither blocks acceptance.

findings.title: printFrontier()'s per-violation branch duplicates frontierRefusalLines()'s requirement==="contract" logic instead of reusing it
findings.evidence: packages/runtime/scripts/rollback-preflight.mjs's printFrontier() still has its own inline ternary — `v.requirement === "contract" ? '...requires the ${v.contract} door contract, which the target does NOT declare' : '...requires ${v.body}, which the target does NOT carry'` — right beside the new packages/runtime/lib/rollback-preflight.mjs export frontierRefusalLines(), which branches on the identical `v.requirement === "contract"` condition to build a related but differently-worded line. The commit that added frontierRefusalLines (36d0b3355) explicitly cites this file's own stated design law for doing so — 'a second inline copy of a rule drifts from the verdict that used it', the same sentence refusalFooterLines and taskIsStranded already justify — but did not apply that same consolidation to printFrontier's own violation loop, which is a second, un-consolidated place carrying the same branch.
findings.required_fix: Judgement call, not required for acceptance. Either factor a small shared 'describe one violation' helper both printFrontier and frontierRefusalLines call, or fold printFrontier's per-violation line into a (verbosity-flag) call to frontierRefusalLines, so the file's own anti-drift argument covers both output paths it currently applies to only one of.

findings.title: Commit 36d0b3355 groups a large batch of new cells with a substantial implementation rewrite in one commit
findings.evidence: git show 36d0b3355 --stat: 4 files, +491/-75, adding 9 new test() cells to packages/runtime/tests/rollback-preflight.test.mjs in the same commit that generalises FRONTIER_BODY_RULES -> FRONTIER_RULES, rewrites verdictOver's reason derivation, rewrites the whole CLI's target-resolution and refusal-printing logic, and edits two-build-cutover-e2e.mjs. WORK-ORDER.md rule 4 asks for 'one slice at a time... commit per green slice or per small group of slices'; this is a single commit covering what reads as several vertical slices (the rule-table shape, the CLI's --supported-contracts handling, the printed refusal text, the two-build drill wiring).
findings.required_fix: Not required for acceptance — this is not the horizontal-slicing anti-pattern the skill actually forbids (tests and implementation land together here, not as a separate all-red-tests-first commit), and the work order explicitly permits 'a small group of slices' per commit; the pieces in this commit are also difficult to green independently since the CLI and the test file both depend on the same table shape. Recorded as a judgement call on slice granularity, not a rework item.
